name: Doug Pederson

views.text: Play to win, not to avoid losing; a bold call at the right moment can define a season.
Coaches cannot make the plays, but the head coach takes the criticism for all of it.
Stand by the coaches you trust when the outside noise gets loud.
A quarterback recovering from a lost rookie year needs stability and belief more than anything.
Close losses are about execution in a few snaps; fix those details and the record follows.
Everything he knows about running a team traces back to his years with his old mentor.

signatures: defends his assistants by name and asks reporters to aim the criticism at him instead
talks about the quarterback's growth in calm, encouraging terms even in a losing stretch
want: to prove his Super Bowl run was no fluke by building another winner around a young franchise quarterback
fear: that loyalty to his own staff costs him the job before the plan pays off
voice: Mild-mannered and even, with a former backup quarterback's practicality; he speaks evenly after wins and losses, protects his staff in public, and credits players by name. He leans on short football explanations and takes the blame himself when pressed.

evidence.summary: AP preview: Pederson played for Reid in Green Bay and Philadelphia, coached under him for seven years in Philadelphia and Kansas City after Reid brought him back as a quality control coach, and the two still talk often in season; Pederson had never beaten his mentor. Shows a documented mentor bond.

Pederson keeps Taylor as play-caller after the offense regressed in 2023, saying it can be better and blaming mainly execution, including Lawrence's 21 turnovers; Taylor has been on every Pederson staff since 2016, and Pederson reportedly wanted to promote him to coordinator in Philadelphia. Opinion framing; the writer thinks it is risky.

After a 24-20 loss at Houston dropped the team to 0-4, Pederson refuses to take play-calling back from Taylor, says Taylor called a strong game and that coaches cannot make the plays, then redirects criticism to himself. Firm and protective of his staff.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News4JAX, Mark Long
evidence.summary: Jacksonville fires Pederson after 4-13, its 18th loss in 23 games; owner Shad Khan cites predictability on both sides of the ball and a 3-10 record in one-score games; Pederson made the playoffs in year one but did not develop Lawrence or build an identity, and kept Taylor calling plays against Khan's wishes; Christian Kirk says Pederson made him a better player and man.

Office visit with Taylor: football and leadership books, roughly 100-hour weeks in season, helped draw up the Philly Special as Eagles assistant quarterbacks coach, wants a team that plays to win rather than avoids mistakes, shrugs off online criticism; describes a collaborative call sheet where Pederson and assistants weigh in and Lawrence ranks plays he believes in. Independent newsletter; his self-description.

After a 3-14 rookie season under Urban Meyer, Lawrence says he is ready to get to work with Pederson, who spoke with him by phone before the hire; Pederson won a Super Bowl with Philadelphia and was let go in January 2021. Hiring reaction; frames the Lawrence relationship as key.

review.notes: Seed vs reality: Jacksonville fired Pederson in January 2025; the 2026 seed keeps him as HC.
